title: The open subfunctor $F$
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], and $\sigma\in X(k)$; regard $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor] as a functor on schemes $T$ over $k$, a morphism $u:T'\to T$ over $k$ acting by $[\mathcal{L}]\mapsto[u_X^*\mathcal{L}]$ with $u_X:X_{T'}\to X_T$ the base change of $u$ [def-pc-base-change]. For a scheme $T$ over $k$, with $f_T:X_T\to T$ the base change of $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $F(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}(T)$ be the subset of those classes $[\mathcal{L}]$ such that $Rf_{T,*}\mathcal{L}$ ($Rf_{T,*}$ as in [def-pc-derived-direct-image]) is an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_T)$ isomorphic to an invertible $\mathcal{O}_T$-module placed in degree $0$ [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero] (a condition depending only on the isomorphism class of $\mathcal{L}$). This defines the assignment $T\mapsto F(T)$ only; that it is stable under the maps $u_X^*$, i.e. is a subfunctor of $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ in the sense of [def-pc-subfunctor], and that the inclusion is representable by open immersions, is Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.6.2 (Tag 0B9V), proved separately; only after that lemma is $F$ called the subfunctor $F$.

lean.statement: def picardInvertibleDirectImageClasses {k : Type v} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [f.IsSmoothProjectiveCurve] (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) [∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), HasInjectiveResolutions (pullback f T.hom).Modules] (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Set ((picardFunctorNormalized f σ hσ).toFunctor.obj (op T))
lean.note: The old picardFunctorInvertibleDirectImage record requires [IsProper f] to construct its Subfunctor, while the dependency node defines only the pointwise assignment F(T). The recorded IsSmoothProjectiveCurve class does not provide a properness instance. This module states that exact pointwise assignment, reusing picardFunctorNormalized and IsInvertibleDirectImage, without a further properness hypothesis or a duplicate derived-image predicate; base-change stability is left to its separate node.
